mathematical_claim: Deleting M0=U_|E|,k is not a drop-in replacement preserving the source proof's per-essential-edge unique-extension witness: a feasible two-terminal series-parallel multigraph has two essential candidate edges outside E_S that both extend the same gammoid-only query, while M0 uniquely selects the requested target. This does not rule out a different joint representative-family theorem.
assumptions: There are terminals a,b and nonterminals u,v; the multigraph has 3 parallel au edges, 2 parallel uv edges e1,e2, and 3 parallel vb edges.
S={a,b}; D={A,B}; tau(a)=A and tau(b)=B is injective; s=3, k=3, q=2.
The metric is the discrete metric mu(A,B)=1, finite, symmetric, positive off diagonal, and triangle-inequality respecting.
The source precheck holds with |E_S|=6=2k; e1,e2 are internal nonterminal-boundary edges, hence outside E_S and inside the source certificate family.
Essentiality uses the source definition: crossing in every tau-extension of cost at most q and crossing count at most k.
The source gammoid construction and its pushing lemma / Proposition 4.8 are used only as stated in the 2018 proof.
verified_steps: For s label slots the source uses M=M1 direct-sum ... direct-sum Ms direct-sum M0, with s gammoid copies of rank |E_S|<=2k and M0=U_|E|,k of rank k; total rank <=(2s+1)k.

For e outside E_S, Y(e) has one sink-copy e'_i in every gammoid layer and original edge element e0 in M0, so p=s+1 and the representative lemma's binomial bound is choose(rank(M),p)=O_s(k^(s+1)) for fixed s.
The source witness has X_i=delta(V_i) union delta(t_i) for i<=r, X_i=delta(V_i) for i>r, and X0=C minus {e}; the uniform coordinate makes the requested edge the unique extension among C.
For the four-vertex series-parallel graph, the four possible a-side sets have cut sizes 3,2,8,3. The unique minimum cut is {a,u}|{v,b}, crossing exactly e1,e2 at cost 2; it is feasible under k=3.

With q=2, every extension of cost at most q and at most k crossings is the unique optimum, so both e1 and e2 are essential. Since E_S comprises the six terminal-incident edges, both target edges are outside E_S.

For the fixed optimum lambda, the gammoid coordinates X1,...,Xs are the same for target e1 and target e2. Applying the source pushing argument to each essential edge shows each target extends every corresponding gammoid restriction; the unused third label has V3 empty.

For target e1, X0={e2}; in U_8,3 the element e1 extends X0 and e2 is blocked by overlap. Swapping targets swaps this unique extension. Thus M0 supplies the source proof's per-edge uniqueness that the gammoid-only tuple lacks.
The earlier all-terminal K3 proposal is ineligible, not a counterexample: all its edges are in E_S, and source tuples Y(e) are defined only for e outside E_S.

For an abstract ground set of m<=k elements, singleton certificates in U_m,k have p=1 and size m; each is necessary by querying all elements except e. This is an identity bound only, not a graph-sparsifier result.

counterexamples.graph: Two-terminal series-parallel multigraph with 3 parallel au edges, 2 parallel uv edges e1,e2, and 3 parallel vb edges; terminals a,b; nonterminals u,v.
counterexamples.cut_check: a-side cut sizes for {a}, {a,u}, {a,v}, {a,u,v} are 3,2,8,3; the unique cost-2 extension crosses exactly e1,e2.
counterexamples.certificate_check: e1,e2 are both essential and outside E_S. They both extend the same gammoid-only witness; for target e1, M0's X0={e2} permits only e1, and conversely for target e2.
counterexamples.scope: Finite obstruction to this layer deletion's source-proof exchange step only; not a lower bound on all reduced representative families or on arbitrary sparsifiers.

independent_review.conclusion: The parallel-bundle graph passes source eligibility and makes two internal edges essential. Deleting M0 makes the gammoid-only extension query non-unique and invalidates the source's per-edge inference. This refutes the specific proof transformation, not every possible compression.
